OPENING.TITLE: Opening the MDT
OPENING.ITEM_HINT: Using the tablet item from the inventory opens the MDT. The item has to exist in your inventory resource already, the MDT doesn't create it.
OPENING.COMMAND_HINT: Typing the command in chat (/mdt by default, set in config.lua) opens the MDT.
OPENING.DESCRIPTION: The ways officers can open the tablet. Keep at least one on. Changes apply right away.
OPENING.ITEM_NAME_HINT: The inventory item that opens the MDT.

DEPARTMENTS.TITLE: Department access
DEPARTMENTS.ENABLED_HINT: On: each record has a visibility (shown in the example below) that decides which departments can open it.
DEPARTMENTS.RECORDS_HINT: Only these record types follow department access. The others stay visible to every department.
DEPARTMENTS.DEFAULT_VISIBILITY_HINT: What a newly created record starts with. The department that owns it can change it on the record afterwards.
DEPARTMENTS.BYPASS_HINT: These jobs see and manage every record, whatever its visibility. Good for chiefs, internal affairs or the court.
DEPARTMENTS.DESCRIPTION: With several departments (police, sheriff, rangers...) you can decide who sees which records. Turned off, every department sees everything.

EXAMPLE.TITLE: Who sees a record
EXAMPLE.HINT: The three visibilities, and who can open a record set to each. The highlighted one is what new records get.

SOCIETY.TITLE: Department funds
SOCIETY.ENABLED: Pay fines into the department account
SOCIETY.ENABLED_HINT: When a charge with a fine is sent, the money goes into the department's society account. Off: the money is just taken from the citizen.

ACCOUNTS.TITLE: Society accounts
ACCOUNTS.DESCRIPTION: The banking account each job's fines are paid into. Leave it empty to use the job name.

CUT.TITLE: Officer share
CUT.ENABLED: Pay officers a share of fines
CUT.ENABLED_HINT: Turn on to set the share below.
CUT.PERCENT_HINT: The part of each fine the officer gets.
CUT.MIN_HINT: The smallest amount an officer gets per charge, even on a small fine. 0 means no minimum.
CUT.MAX_HINT: The largest amount an officer gets per charge, even on a huge fine. 0 means no limit.
CUT.PAYMENT_TYPE_HINT: Whether the officer's share goes to their cash or their bank account.
CUT.DESCRIPTION: Give the officer who sent a charge a share of its fine, as a reward. The rest goes to the department. Only for fines taken straight from the bank; billing scripts pay their own commission.

EXAMPLE.TITLE: Try a fine
EXAMPLE.HINT: Type a fine to see how it's split with the current settings.

SOCIETY.FUNDS_PAYMENT_TYPE_HINT: Where an officer's own money comes from or goes to when they deposit into or withdraw from department funds on the Management page.

BILLING.TITLE: Billing
BILLING.ALLOW_DEBT_HINT: When a citizen can't afford a fine taken straight from the bank. On: their balance goes below zero. Off: the fine is skipped and nobody gets paid.
BILLING.DUE_HINT: For billing scripts with due dates (vms_cityhall). Others ignore it.
BILLING.DESCRIPTION: How fines are collected. Without a billing script the fine is taken from the citizen's bank right away.

DATA.TITLE: Citizens & vehicles
DATA.AUTO_POPULATE_HINT: On: the Citizens and Vehicles pages show every player and vehicle in your framework. Off: nothing shows until an officer registers it by hand (for strict roleplay servers).
DATA.BANK_HINT: Shows each citizen's bank account number and balance on their record. Only works if your framework adapter supports it.
DATA.PHONE_RECORDS_HINT: Shows the phone records button (calls and messages) next to a citizen's phone number. Turn off if your server doesn't want officers reading phone data.
DATA.RESIDENTS: Show who lives at a property
DATA.RESIDENTS_HINT: Shows tenants and co-owners on property records, when your housing resource provides them.

LIMITS.TITLE: Limits
LIMITS.MAX_TAGS_HINT: The most tags (like "Armed" or "Gang member") one record can have. Lowering it doesn't remove tags already added.

LOGS.TITLE: Activity log
LOGS.RETENTION_HINT: Logs older than this are deleted, right away when you lower it. 0 keeps them forever (the database keeps growing). Logs already sent to Discord or another service aren't touched.

IMAGES.TITLE: Images
IMAGES.HOSTS_HINT: Only links from these sites (and their subdomains) are accepted. Leave it empty to allow any site. Pasting a full link adds just its site.
IMAGES.DESCRIPTION: Rules for image links officers attach to records (mugshots, evidence photos, galleries).

TESTER.TITLE: Try a link
TESTER.HINT: Paste an image link to see if officers could attach it with the current rules.
TESTER.OK: Allowed — officers can attach this link.
TESTER.TOO_LONG: Refused — the link is too long.
TESTER.NOT_A_LINK: Refused — that isn't an http(s) link.
TESTER.NOT_ALLOWED: Refused — that site isn't on the allowed list.

COLLAB.TITLE: Live collaboration
COLLAB.ENABLED_HINT: Officers can invite each other into a record and see each other's changes as they type.
COLLAB.EXPIRY_HINT: An invite nobody answers is cancelled after this long. 0 means it never expires.

OPERATIONS.TITLE: Operation plans
OPERATIONS.DESCRIPTION: Limits for the drawings on a warrant's operation plan map. They keep a single plan from becoming too heavy to load.
OPERATIONS.SHAPES_HINT: The most markers, lines and areas one plan can have.
OPERATIONS.POINTS_HINT: The most points one line or area can have. Freehand drawings use the most.

MODIFICATIONS.TITLE: Vehicle modification categories
MODIFICATIONS.DESCRIPTION: The categories officers pick when they log a known modification on a vehicle (a tuned engine, hidden compartment...). Mark the illegal ones as contraband so they stand out.
MODIFICATIONS.LIST_HINT: A category that's already used can't be deleted, turn it off instead.

LIST_FIELDS.NAME: Internal name
LIST_FIELDS.NAME_HINT: Saved on every record that uses it. Lowercase letters, numbers, _ and - only. Filled in from the label for you.
LIST_FIELDS.LABEL: Label
LIST_FIELDS.LABEL_HINT: What officers see. Changing it renames the entry everywhere, old records included.
LIST_FIELDS.DISABLED_HINT: Hidden when officers pick one for a new record. Records that already use it keep it.
LIST_FIELDS.FLAGGED_HINT: Modifications in this category get a red "Flagged" mark on the vehicle page.

REGION.TITLE: Language & formats
REGION.DESCRIPTION: Server defaults. Every officer can still pick their own language, currency and formats in their MDT settings; these are what someone gets before they do.
REGION.LOCALE_HINT: Used for messages shown in the game (notifications, cameras) and logs, and as the MDT language for officers who haven't picked one.
REGION.CURRENCY_HINT: The currency fines, bank balances and department funds are shown in.
REGION.PHONE_HINT: A template for phone numbers: {3} means "3 digits go here", anything else is shown as typed. ({3}) {3}-{4} turns 5551234567 into (555) 123-4567.
REGION.DATE_HINT: How dates are written everywhere in the MDT.
REGION.WEEK_START_HINT: The day calendars and weekly schedules start on.
REGION.NUMBER_HINT: Whether thousands are separated with commas or dots.
REGION.MEASUREMENT_HINT: Imperial (feet, miles, pounds) or metric (meters, kilometers, kilograms) for distances, heights and weights.

EXAMPLE.TITLE: How it looks
EXAMPLE.HINT: Sample values with the current settings.

STATUSES.TITLE: Officer statuses
STATUSES.LIST_HINT: Add your own or change the color, icon and name of any status. Turned-off or deleted statuses disappear from the status menu and officers using one are moved to the default status.
STATUSES.LIST_LOCKED: This is the default status, so it can't be turned off or deleted. Pick another default status first.

LIST_FIELDS.NAME: Internal name
LIST_FIELDS.NAME_HINT: Lowercase letters, numbers, _ and - only. Filled in from the label for you.
LIST_FIELDS.LABEL: Label
LIST_FIELDS.LABEL_HINT: What officers see. Leave it empty on a built-in status to keep its translated name in every language.
LIST_FIELDS.COLOR_HINT: Used for the icon and the dot next to an officer.
LIST_FIELDS.ICON_HINT: Any Lucide icon name from lucide.dev/icons, e.g. siren, dog or coffee.
LIST_FIELDS.GROUP_HINT: Where it's listed in the status menu.
LIST_FIELDS.DISABLED_HINT: Officers can't pick it. Officers using it are moved to the default status.

STATUSES.DEFAULT_HINT: The status an officer gets when they go on duty, and the one officers fall back to when theirs is turned off.
STATUSES.DESCRIPTION: The statuses officers can set on themselves (available, busy, on scene...), shown to everyone on the roster and the map.

CALLSIGNS.TITLE: Callsigns
CALLSIGNS.DESCRIPTION: How callsigns look for each rank, where they have to be unique, and when officers get one automatically.
CALLSIGNS.RULES_HINT: Every # is one digit of a number that counts up: "1-ADAM-##" hands out 1-ADAM-01, 1-ADAM-02... Officers can only use callsigns that fit their rank's format. When several rules cover a rank, the most specific one wins.

RULES_FIELDS.FORMAT_HINT: One group of # (up to 4) for the number, e.g. "1-ADAM-##" or "M-###".
RULES_FIELDS.JOBS_HINT: Leave empty for every whitelisted job.

CALLSIGNS.UNIQUE_HINT: Who can't share a callsign. Every department and each department also check officers who are offline.
CALLSIGNS.SELF_EDIT_HINT: Off: only managers (employees.manage) can change callsigns, from the Employees page.
CALLSIGNS.ASSIGN_HIRE_HINT: New recruits get the next free callsign of their rank.
CALLSIGNS.ASSIGN_RANK_HINT: An officer whose callsign doesn't fit their new rank's format gets the next free one of it.
CALLSIGNS.ASSIGN_DUTY_HINT: Officers going on duty without a callsign, or with one that doesn't fit their rank, get one.
CALLSIGNS.MAX_LENGTH_HINT: The longest callsign an officer can have (e.g. "2-ADAM-12" is 9 characters).

EXAMPLE.TITLE: Callsigns per rank
EXAMPLE.HINT: The format each rank follows and the first callsign it hands out.

NATIONALITIES.TITLE: Nationalities
NATIONALITIES.LIST_HINT: The choices when registering a citizen and in the Citizens page filter. Removing one doesn't change citizens who already have it.

CHARGES.TITLE: Charge limits
CHARGES.DESCRIPTION: The most one penal code charge can carry. They stop typos like an extra zero; the penal code editor and every charge respect them.
CHARGES.QUANTITY: Times a charge can be stacked
CHARGES.QUANTITY_HINT: For charges that can be added more than once (e.g. 3× Assault), the highest number allowed.
CHARGES.FINE_HINT: The most one charge can fine, per count.
CHARGES.JAIL_HINT: The most jail time one charge can give, per count.
CHARGES.COMMUNITY_SERVICE_HINT: The most community service one charge can give, per count.
CHARGES.BAIL_HINT: The most bail one charge can set, per count.
CHARGES.POINTS_HINT: The most driver's license points one charge can add, per count.

POINTS.TITLE: License points
POINTS.ENABLED_HINT: Off: points are ignored and hidden everywhere in the MDT.
POINTS.WINDOW_HINT: Only points from charges in this period count. Older points expire on their own.
POINTS.THRESHOLD_HINT: A license is suspended once its points reach this total.
POINTS.DESCRIPTION: Traffic charges can add points to a citizen's driver's license. Too many points within the counting period and the license shows as suspended.

PRESETS.OFF_HINT: Licenses are never suspended by points

EXAMPLE.TITLE: Example driver
EXAMPLE.HINT: Set how many points a citizen has (from the last {{days}} days) to see where they stand.
EXAMPLE.VALID: License valid — {{left}} more points until it's suspended.

STASH.TITLE: Evidence storage
STASH.DESCRIPTION: Items an officer logs on an evidence record are moved out of their inventory into a storage made for that record. Changes apply to storages created after you save.
STASH.LABEL: Storage name
STASH.LABEL_HINT: What the storage is called in the inventory. %s is replaced with the evidence number and has to be in the name once.
STASH.SLOTS_HINT: How many different items one evidence record can hold.
STASH.WEIGHT_HINT: In your inventory's own unit. ox, qb and ps inventory count grams, so 100000 is 100 kg.
STASH.WEIGHT_PREVIEW: On ox, qb or ps inventory that's {{weight}}.

TYPES.TITLE: Evidence types
TYPES.DESCRIPTION: The kinds of evidence officers pick from when they log evidence, like firearm or narcotics. Each record has one type; use tags for extra details.
TYPES.LIST_HINT: A type that's already used can't be deleted, turn it off instead. At least one has to stay on.

LIST_FIELDS.NAME: Internal name
LIST_FIELDS.NAME_HINT: Saved on every record that uses it. Lowercase letters, numbers, _ and - only. Filled in from the label for you.
LIST_FIELDS.LABEL: Label
LIST_FIELDS.LABEL_HINT: What officers see. Changing it renames the entry everywhere, old records included.
LIST_FIELDS.DISABLED_HINT: Hidden when officers pick one for a new record. Records that already use it keep it.

ANALYSES.TITLE: Lab analyses
ANALYSES.DESCRIPTION: The tests officers can request on a piece of evidence, like DNA or ballistics. Officers with the lab permission record the results.
ANALYSES.LIST_HINT: An analysis that's already been requested can't be deleted, turn it off instead. At least one has to stay on.

LIST_FIELDS.NAME: Internal name
LIST_FIELDS.NAME_HINT: Saved on every record that uses it. Lowercase letters, numbers, _ and - only. Filled in from the label for you.
LIST_FIELDS.LABEL: Label
LIST_FIELDS.LABEL_HINT: What officers see. Changing it renames the entry everywhere, old records included.
LIST_FIELDS.DISABLED_HINT: Hidden when officers pick one for a new record. Records that already use it keep it.

CHAT.TITLE: Chat
CHAT.SLOWDOWN_HINT: An officer has to wait this long between two messages. Stops channels from being flooded. 0 turns it off.
CHAT.RETENTION_HINT: Messages older than this are deleted, right away when you lower it. 0 keeps them forever.
CHAT.LIVE_LOCATION_HINT: A shared live location stops if the officer sharing it sends no update for this long (crash, disconnect). It updates about every 8 seconds, so keep this higher.

DMS.TITLE: Direct messages
DMS.ENABLED_HINT: Officers can have private 1-to-1 chats. Only the two of them can read those.
DMS.CROSS_JOB_HINT: On: officers can message anyone with MDT access. Off: only colleagues with the same job.

EVENTS.TITLE: Automatic posts
EVENTS.DESCRIPTION: Things the MDT posts to a chat channel on its own, so nobody misses them. Pick the channel for each, or turn it off.
EVENTS.OFFICER_PANIC_HINT: An officer pressed their panic button.
EVENTS.BOLO_CREATED_HINT: A BOLO (be on the lookout) was created.
EVENTS.BOLO_LOCATED_HINT: A BOLO was marked as found.
EVENTS.RADAR_PLATE_HIT_HINT: The plate reader spotted a vehicle with a BOLO or warrant.

RADIO.TITLE: Radio codes
RADIO.FORMATS_HINT: The shapes a radio code (10-codes) has to follow when one is created or edited: d is a digit, a is a letter, anything else stays as typed. d-dd allows 10-4. Empty allows any code.

TESTER.TITLE: Try a code
TESTER.HINT: Type a code to see whether it would be accepted.
TESTER.ANY: Accepted — no formats are set, so any code is allowed.
TESTER.NO_MATCH: Refused — it doesn't match any of the formats above.

CHANNELS.TITLE: Chat channels
CHANNELS.DESCRIPTION: The channels in the MDT chat. Each can be open to every department or only some, and posting can be limited to ranks with a permission (everyone else still reads it).
CHANNELS.LIST_HINT: A channel that an automatic chat post goes to (below) has to be moved first before it can be deleted.

LIST_FIELDS.ID_HINT: Messages are saved under it. Lowercase letters, numbers, _ and - only.
LIST_FIELDS.NAME: Channel name
LIST_FIELDS.NAME_HINT: What officers see on the tab, shown as #name.
LIST_FIELDS.JOBS_HINT: Who can read and write in it.
LIST_FIELDS.POSTPERMISSION_HINT: Optional. Only ranks with this permission can write; everyone else in the departments above can only read. Good for announcements.

NOTIFICATIONS.TITLE: Notifications
NOTIFICATIONS.DESCRIPTION: What lands in the bell on the dashboard. Personal ones wait for officers who are offline; department-wide ones only reach officers online at the time.
NOTIFICATIONS.RETENTION_HINT: Notifications older than this are deleted, right away when you lower it. 0 keeps them forever.

CALLS.TITLE: Dispatch calls
CALLS.REQUIRE_DUTY_HINT: On: new calls only reach officers who are on duty. Off: every officer with MDT access gets them.
CALLS.EXTERNAL_HINT: With another dispatch resource (ps-dispatch, cd_dispatch...), also show the MDT's own popup and sound for the calls it sends. Off: they only appear in the MDT and on the map.
CALLS.DURATION_HINT: How long a new call's popup stays on screen before the next one shows.
CALLS.LIFETIME_HINT: A call nobody responds to closes on its own after this long. Robberies and heists have their own, longer time in config.lua.
CALLS.HISTORY_HINT: How many closed calls stay in the dispatch history. 0 keeps none.
CALLS.FLOOR_HINT: The least time between two automatic alerts from the same player, whatever the type. Protects against alert spam.

ESCALATION.TITLE: Escalation
ESCALATION.ENABLED_HINT: Off: a call keeps the priority it was created with.
ESCALATION.LOW_HINT: How long a low priority call waits before it becomes medium.
ESCALATION.MEDIUM_HINT: How long it then waits as medium before it becomes high.
ESCALATION.DESCRIPTION: Calls nobody responds to can move up in priority over time, so they get noticed.

EXAMPLE.TITLE: Timeline of an unanswered low call
EXAMPLE.HINT: From the moment the call comes in.

BLIPS.TITLE: Map blips
BLIPS.ENABLED_HINT: On-duty officers see a map marker for every open call. Turning it off removes them right away.
BLIPS.SHORT_RANGE_HINT: Markers only show on the minimap when close to the officer.
BLIPS.COLOUR_HINT: Markers take their priority's color below instead of the call type's own.
BLIPS.DEFAULT_HINT: Used by call types without a marker of their own (calls from other scripts, new types).
BLIPS.PULSE_HINT: A ring under the marker of call types that have it turned on, so important calls stand out.
BLIPS.PULSE_UNTIL_ASSIGNED: Only until a unit is attached
BLIPS.PULSE_UNTIL_ASSIGNED_HINT: The ring goes away once someone takes the call.
BLIPS.FLASH_HINT: How long a new call's marker flashes. 0 means it doesn't flash.
BLIPS.FADE_EXPIRY_HINT: A call nobody took dims over this long before it closes on its own. 0 turns it off.
BLIPS.FADE_HINT: How long a closed call's marker takes to disappear. 0 removes it at once.

UNITS.TITLE: Officer blips
UNITS.DESCRIPTION: On-duty officers see the other officers on duty on the game map and minimap, with an icon for how they move and a color per department. Nearby officers' blips follow them smoothly; far away ones move with each position update.
UNITS.ENABLED_HINT: Turning it off removes the blips right away.
UNITS.OTHER_DEPARTMENTS_HINT: Off: officers only see officers of their own department.
UNITS.SHORT_RANGE_HINT: Blips only show on the minimap when close.
UNITS.SPRITE_FOOT_HINT: Shows which way the officer faces.
UNITS.COLOUR_HINT: The color of every department that doesn't have its own below.
UNITS.JOB_COLOURS_HINT: Give a department its own color, so officers can tell units apart.

CHANCE.TITLE: Report chance
CHANCE.ENABLED_HINT: Off: every automatic alert reaches dispatch.
CHANCE.BASE_CHANCE_HINT: The chance a crime is reported when nobody is around.
CHANCE.WITNESS_BONUS_HINT: Each person nearby adds this much. 3 witnesses with 20% each add 60%.
CHANCE.MAX_CHANCE_HINT: However many witnesses there are, the chance never goes above this (without a camera).
CHANCE.SILENCED_MULTIPLIER_HINT: A shot from a suppressed weapon keeps only this much of the chance. 15% turns an 80% chance into 12%.
CHANCE.NIGHT_START_HOUR_HINT: In-game hour (0-23) from which fewer crimes are noticed.
CHANCE.NIGHT_END_HOUR_HINT: In-game hour (0-23) when the night penalty stops.
CHANCE.NIGHT_MULTIPLIER_HINT: At night the chance keeps only this much. 50% halves it.
CHANCE.CAMERA_BONUS_HINT: Added when a working CCTV camera sees the crime.
CHANCE.CAMERA_MIN_CHANCE_HINT: A crime a camera sees is reported at least this often. 100% means always.
CHANCE.DESCRIPTION: In real life not every crime gets reported. With this on, automatic alerts (shooting, car theft...) only reach dispatch with a chance that depends on witnesses, the time of day and cameras. Use the simulator below to see the result.

PRESETS.VERY_REALISTIC_HINT: Few crimes reach dispatch without witnesses or cameras

SIMULATOR.TITLE: Simulator
SIMULATOR.HINT: Set up a crime to see how likely it is to be reported with the current settings.
SIMULATOR.RESULT_one: About {{count}} out of 10 crimes like this would be reported.
SIMULATOR.RESULT_other: About {{count}} out of 10 crimes like this would be reported.
SIMULATOR.ALWAYS: Report chance is off, so every crime is reported.

ALERTS.TITLE: Automatic alerts
ALERTS.DESCRIPTION: Alerts the game raises on its own when a player commits a crime. Map blip: the icon and color of the call's marker. Cooldown: how long before the same player can trigger that alert again. On-duty exempt: officers on duty never trigger it (e.g. speeding during a pursuit). Departments: who receives the alert; all departments when none is picked.

SCENE.TITLE: Scene info
SCENE.ENABLED_HINT: Robbery and heist calls say how many people were around the caller, so officers know what to expect.
SCENE.RADIUS_HINT: People within this distance of the caller are counted.

RADAR.TITLE: Plate reader
RADAR.COOLDOWN_HINT: How long before the same plate warns the same officer again.
RADAR.THRESHOLD_HINT: A match with a BOLO or warrant of this priority or higher also creates a dispatch call for everyone.
RADAR.AUTO_LOCK: Lock the plate on a match
RADAR.AUTO_LOCK_HINT: The radar locks the plate that matched, so the officer doesn't lose it.
RADAR.DESCRIPTION: With a radar resource (wk_wars2x), every plate the radar reads is checked against BOLOs and warrants, and the officer is warned on a match.

DAMAGE.TITLE: Damage
DAMAGE.DESTROYABLE_HINT: Off: shooting a camera does nothing.
DAMAGE.LINE_OF_SIGHT: Shooter has to see the camera
DAMAGE.LINE_OF_SIGHT_HINT: Hits only count when nothing is between the shooter and the camera. Stops damage through walls.
DAMAGE.HEALTH_HINT: How much damage a camera takes before it breaks. Changing it keeps every camera at the same share of its health.
DAMAGE.WEAPON_DAMAGE_HINT: For weapons that aren't in the weapon list.
DAMAGE.REPORT_DISTANCE_HINT: Hits from farther than this are ignored.
DAMAGE.REPAIR_DISTANCE_HINT: How close a player has to stand to repair a broken camera.
DAMAGE.DESCRIPTION: CCTV cameras can be shot and broken. A broken camera goes offline until someone repairs it.

EXAMPLE.TITLE: How tough a camera is
EXAMPLE.HINT: With weapons that use the default damage.

MODELS.TITLE: Models
MODELS.DESCRIPTION: Every prop that can be placed as a CCTV camera, and what its feed can do. Tune a model in game to see each change on the prop as you make it.
MODELS.LIST_HINT: Add custom props by their model name. A model that placed cameras still use can't be removed.
MODELS.TUNE_HINT: Places this prop in front of you and shows its feed with every change, before you save.
MODELS.EDIT_DESCRIPTION: What a feed from this prop can do. Placed cameras pick up changes the next time someone opens their feed.

FIELDS.LENS_OFFSET_HINT: Moves the view forward off the prop. Raise it if the mount shows in the feed.
FIELDS.MOVEABLE_HINT: Off: the feed stays exactly as the camera was placed.
FIELDS.PITCH_MIN_HINT: How far down it can look. -90 is straight down.
FIELDS.PITCH_MAX_HINT: How far up it can look. 90 is straight up.
FIELDS.YAW_LIMIT_HINT: How far it turns to each side of the way it was placed.
FIELDS.ZOOM_HINT: Off: the feed keeps the default view.
FIELDS.FOV_MIN_HINT: Field of view fully zoomed in. Lower is closer.
FIELDS.FOV_MAX_HINT: Field of view fully zoomed out. Higher is wider.
FIELDS.NIGHTVISION_HINT: Offers night vision on its feed.

WEAPONS.TITLE: Weapons
WEAPONS.DESCRIPTION: Which weapons can damage cameras, and how much. A weapon only does damage when its group is on and it isn't blocked in the list.
WEAPONS.GROUPS_HINT: Only weapons from groups that are on can damage cameras.
WEAPONS.DAMAGE_HINT: Damage for specific weapons. Hits are kept between 10 and 50. Block a weapon to stop it from damaging cameras even when its group is on. Weapons not listed use the default damage per hit.
WEAPONS.BROWSE_DESCRIPTION: Click a weapon to add it with the default damage ({{damage}}), or click it again to remove it. Addon weapons from your inventory are listed too, and you can type any weapon name.
WEAPONS.EMPTY: No weapons yet. Every weapon uses the default damage per hit.
WEAPONS.GROUP_OFF: The {{group}} group is off, so this weapon can't damage cameras.
WEAPONS.UNKNOWN: Not a GTA weapon or a weapon item in your inventory. Check that the name is correct.

CAPTURE.TITLE: Photos & previews
CAPTURE.ENABLED_HINT: An automatic alert near a working camera is linked to it, so officers can open the feed from the call.
CAPTURE.SCREENSHOT: Attach a photo of the scene
CAPTURE.SCREENSHOT_HINT: The call also gets a photo of the moment.
CAPTURE.PREVIEW_HINT: The Cameras page shows a recent still image of each camera.
CAPTURE.PREVIEW_REFRESH_HINT: How old a preview can get before the next officer viewing the camera takes a new one.
CAPTURE.RADIUS_HINT: An alert is linked to a working camera this close to the offender.
CAPTURE.LINE_OF_SIGHT: Camera has to see the offender
CAPTURE.LINE_OF_SIGHT_HINT: Only link a camera that's pointed at the offender with nothing in between. Turn off if your custom camera props face the wrong way.
CAPTURE.FOV_HINT: How wide a camera sees. The offender has to be inside this angle.
CAPTURE.VIEW_RANGE_HINT: How far a camera sees, separate from the search radius.

DASHCAM.TITLE: Dashcams
DASHCAM.MODELS_HINT: Vehicles a dashcam can be turned on in. Add them from the list, from the vehicle you sit in, or by pointing at one in game.
DASHCAM.FRONT_SEATS_HINT: Only the driver or front passenger can turn the dashcam on or off.
DASHCAM.METHOD_HINT: Using the dashcam item, typing the command, or either one. The command still needs the item in their inventory.
DASHCAM.STREAM_RADIUS_HINT: While someone watches a dashcam, players and vehicles this close to the car stay visible in the feed. Bigger shows more but syncs more players to the viewer.
DASHCAM.ITEM_HINT: The inventory item officers use to turn a dashcam on.

HACKING.TITLE: Hacking
HACKING.DISTANCE_HINT: How close a player has to stand to hack a camera and take it offline.
HACKING.COMMAND_HINT: Players can type the hack command near a camera to take it offline. Off: only your own scripts can hack cameras.

RECORDING.TITLE: Recordings
RECORDING.DURATION_HINT: Camera recordings stop and save on their own after this long.
RECORDING.SIZE_HINT: Recordings stop and save when they reach this size, and bigger uploads are refused.
RECORDING.VOICES_HINT: Recordings include players talking near the camera. Each of those players gets FiveM's microphone prompt once. Game sounds are never recorded.
RECORDING.VOICE_RADIUS_HINT: Players talking this close to the camera are recorded.
